VIEW

The senior view: quality is priced in

↑

RBC is a high-return franchise with a strong Canadian banking anchor and significant wealth and capital-markets earnings. At the dated C$280.01 price, our base operating case supports only a modest prospective return. The question is how much persistence investors should pay for.

Research stanceNeutral / watchlistValuation-sensitive; independent judgment
12-month model valueC$279October 2027 · FY2027 EPS 18 ×15.5
Base total return+2.2%Includes assumed C$7.04 cash dividends
10% modeled-return entryC$260Unchanged base outcome; not a timing forecast

Why the business deserves a premium

Distribution scale, relationship deposits, Canadian banking efficiency and wealth referrals can sustain excess returns. Q3 adjusted ROE reached 18.1%, efficiency was 52.2%, and CET1 held at 13.5%. These are substantive advantages.

Why the starting price matters

Our FY2027 adjusted EPS forecast already grows 8.7%. Yet a still-premium 15.5× exit multiple gives C$279, close to today’s price. Strong operating results can coexist with an ordinary shareholder return when the starting valuation is demanding.

What would change the stance?

Durable EPS above C$19.5 with credit and capital intact would challenge our caution. Sustainable ROE below 16%, worsening client economics or rising capital intensity would weaken the franchise-premium thesis. A lower price improves value only if the earnings power survives.

Analysis expanded 18 October 2026. Financials through 31 July; price 16 October. Forecasts, exit multiples, return hurdles and scenario weights below are TickerLantern assumptions. This is independent research, with no investment-bank affiliation or personalized suitability assessment.

EARN

Earnings quality: separate the engines and definitions

↑

RBC’s C$6.024bn reported Q3 income rose 11.3% year over year. Wealth Management and Capital Markets generated C$2.986bn,49.6% of group income. Both contain recurring businesses, but asset prices, activity and issuance can move together. Personal Banking income fell C$15m and Insurance C$50m, so growth was not uniform.

Three earnings denominators, not interchangeable measures
TTM earnings basisEPSP/E at C$280.01Interpretation
IFRS reported dilutedC$15.8617.66×Reported earnings
Issuer-adjusted, derivedC$16.1117.38×Primary comparable earnings anchor
Morningstar normalizedC$16.5816.89×Provider-specific; full adjustment bridge unavailable

Issuer-adjusted bridge: FY2025 EPS 14.43 − prior nine-month 10.58 + current nine-month 12.26 = TTM16.11. Q3 reported EPS 4.23 becomes 4.28 after excluding C$77m after-tax acquisition-intangible amortization; no HSBC integration-cost adjustment is present for this quarter.

Why Morningstar revenue differs from the issuer

The captured quarter shows revenue C$18.511bn versus issuer C$18.538bn. Its combined expense/other-income line is also C$27m lower. That C$27m equals joint-venture/associate income, leaving pretax income unchanged at C$7.749bn. Our operating model uses the issuer revenue/expense classification consistently. This is a presentation reconciliation, not evidence of an accounting error.

Domestic strength, fee sensitivity and execution options

↑

Do not mistake group margin mix for deposit-franchise failure

Group NIM fell to 1.49% from 1.61% a year earlier, partly reflecting trading assets and funding mix. Canadian NIM 2.96% and the group ratio excluding trading 2.07% help distinguish franchise economics from denominator changes. Commercial average deposits rose 9%; pricing and relationship quality remain essential.

HSBC: the next increment is revenue execution

Morningstar describes the C$740m cost-synergy target as achieved in FY2025, and a C$300m revenue-synergy objective by end-2027 with one-third realized in FY2025. These are provider-reported objectives. Existing savings are already in the earnings base; the forecast contains no separate acquisition premium or automatic addition of the full target.

CNB can provide upside through better efficiency and deeper wealth/commercial relationships. We require recurring progress after necessary compliance and risk spending. A deposit increase bought through higher pricing would be less valuable than durable client relationships.

CREDIT

Credit and capital: resilience has a price

↑

Credit is normalizing

Credit stock, flows and reserve measures
IndicatorCurrent / comparison
Q3 total / impaired PCL36 /35bps
Nine-month total PCL38bps versus 45bps prior year
Nine-month impaired PCL37bps in both years
Gross impaired loansC$10.143bn;91bps versus 85bps a year earlier
Allowance / loans70bps versus 74bps a year earlier

Lower performing provisions support year-to-date earnings. Rising impaired loans alongside lower allowance/loan ratios deserve scrutiny, but do not alone establish inadequate reserves. Collateral, recovery assumptions and scenario weights are required.

Housing averages are not the tail

Residential secured lending totals C$479bn, with C$418bn uninsured. Calculated current LTV is 56% overall and 54% uninsured. Those averages provide context, not protection for every borrower.

Personal Canada mortgage impaired PCL is 3bps; credit-card impaired PCL is 333bps on a much smaller C$27.3bn average balance. Loss severity and unsecured exposure matter alongside housing volumes. Greater Toronto 58% and Greater Vancouver 52% in the LTV table are LTVs, not geographic portfolio weights.

How much capital is actually available?

Arithmetic headroom, not immediately distributable cash
Comparison levelGap from 13.5% CET1At fixed C$777.987bn RWA
RBC rounded formal requirement 11.1%240bpsC$18.67bn
Operating-range lower end 12.5%100bpsC$7.78bn
Illustrative midpoint 13.0%50bpsC$3.89bn
Operating-range upper end 13.5%0bpsC$0.00bn

RBC’s 11.1% includes its countercyclical increment; OSFI’s generic large-bank expectation is 11.0%. Management’s operating range is 12.5–13.5%. Earnings added 80bps in Q3; dividends used 34bps, RWA growth 30bps and buybacks 21bps, leaving CET1 flat. Growth and distributions compete for capital generation.

Liquidity adds resilience: LCR125%, NSFR112%, high-quality liquid assets about C$487bn against modeled 30-day outflows C$389bn. Leverage, resolution rules, stress buffers and approvals also constrain distributions. Capital strength does not prevent the equity multiple from falling.

DIST

Dividends and repurchases: do not double count

↑
Different dividend periods answer different questions
MeasureReadingPeriod / assumption
Trailing dividends / yieldC$6.58 /2.35%Trailing payments
Current quarterly / annualized rateC$1.76 /C$7.04Four future payments at current rate assumed
Run-rate payout on FY2026E42.5%7.04 /own EPS 16.56
Run-rate payout on FY2027E39.1%7.04 /own EPS 18.00

Management targets a 40–50% payout, closer to the midpoint. A flat C$7.04 annual rate is just below 40% of our FY2027 estimate, leaving possible room for growth if capital and earnings permit. We keep dividends flat across valuation cases to make their assumptions comparable; future declarations remain discretionary.

At 2.895× book, a buyback can raise EPS while reducing book per remaining share. Repurchasing 1% of starting shares at C$280.01 lifts EPS 1.01% with unchanged profit before lost interest, but reduces BVPS 1.91%. Accretion alone does not establish attractive capital deployment.

Q3 returned approximately C$4.0bn: C$1.6bn repurchases and C$2.4bn common dividends. Our FY2027 average share count declines 1.5%; a rough 21m-share reduction at C$280 would cost C$5.9bn. That is a proxy, not an executed-buyback forecast. Our EPS already reflects fewer shares, so no extra buyback yield is added to total return.

Inspect the buyback arithmetic
After 1% repurchase: BVPS = (B − 0.01 × P) / 0.99
EPS with unchanged income = original EPS / 0.99
B = C$96.7257; P = C$280.01

This isolates arithmetic before foregone investment income, tax, execution price, capital limits or changes in profit.

FY2026 is largely earned; FY2027 is the harder test

FY2026 EPS 16.56 implies Q4 around 4.30 after 12.26 earned in nine months. Revenue 72.5bn implies Q4 revenue 18.55bn, close to Q3’s 18.54bn, adjusted expenses 9.72bn and PCL 1.00bn. The model does not need a sharp year-end acceleration.

FY2027 EPS 18.00 grows 8.7%. Revenue and adjusted expenses both grow about 7.6%, leaving efficiency broadly flat while dollar operating profit rises. PCL increases 0.5bn, and the lower share count contributes roughly 1.5% relative to a flat-share case. Continued fee growth and a stable domestic franchise are needed.

FY2028 EPS 19.28 grows 7.1% despite credit costs reaching 6.0bn, about 48bps of our average loans. This is a late-cycle test, not an issuer loss forecast. Revenue growth and 52.1% efficiency must offset the credit increase; simultaneous weak markets and credit could prevent that.

VALUE

Valuation: earnings power and the duration of ROE

↑

Base: EPS 18 ×15.5 = C$279

From C$280.01, price return is −0.4%; C$7.04 dividends bring total return to +2.2%. Horizon: approximately October 2027, when FY2027 is almost fully earned. This exit P/E is applied to FY2027 earnings; it does not automatically roll forward to FY2028.

Our 15.5× multiple retains a franchise premium while allowing some normalization from 17.38× issuer-adjusted TTM earnings. For a 10% total return, the same multiple needs EPS 19.42,7.9% above our base; or EPS 18 needs 16.72×. A C$260.04 entry would meet that hurdle to the unchanged base outcome.

12-month senior cases; weights are judgments, not calibrated probabilities
Case / judgment weightFY2027 EPSExit P/EPrice valueWith C$7.04 dividends
Bear /30%C$15.0013.0×C$195.00-27.8%
Base /50%C$18.0015.5×C$279.00+2.2%
Bull /20%C$19.5017.0×C$331.50+20.9%

Bear: weaker fees, credit stress and a lower confidence multiple can occur together. Base: moderate growth, operating discipline and manageable credit. Bull: sustained wealth/markets activity, CNB progress and resilient credit support both higher EPS and a high multiple. Constant dividends are an assumption even in stress.

The illustrative weighted price is C$264.30 and weighted total return-3.1%. The 30/50/20 weights are not measured probabilities, confidence intervals or fall-risk estimates; they make the downside/upside tradeoff explicit.

Common book asks a different question

Common BVPS C$96.73 and sustainable ROE 18.1%, required equity return 9.5%, perpetual growth 5% imply P/B 2.911×, or C$281.58 current value. At the reference price, the same equation requires 18.03% perpetual ROE. Our 9.5% return is a judgmental equity hurdle; Morningstar uses 8.2% in its own different framework.

Retention must fund growth:5/18.1=27.6%, leaving 72.4% eventual total equity distributions through dividends and net repurchases. This is not a cash-dividend-only model. Above-book buybacks, OCI, acquisitions and regulatory capital complicate its clean-surplus approximation.

18.1% ROE persistsC$281.58Current steady-state illustration
ROE fades to 16% over 5 yearsC$240.89Same 5% book growth /9.5% required return

A profitable bank can lose material justified value when excess returns fade. The book check is not a 12-month target and is not averaged with C$279. Both methods depend on durable returns and risk premiums; their agreement is not independent validation.

Morningstar’s current fair-value opinion is C$257, with its widget dated 8 September and article 22 September. C$280.01 is 9.0% above that value; moving to 257 would be an 8.2% price decline. It is not a one-year broker target. Our forecasts, multiples and timing are separate.

Underwriting status and missing evidence

This is a conditional public-equity initiation. Reported issuer earnings/capital have strong source support within unaudited interim reporting. Forecast and valuation confidence is lower because persistence, credit and discount assumptions are uncertain. Verified ownership flows, granular credit-vintage tails, a fully normalized current Big Six forecast model, and a complete CET1/RWA projection remain gaps.

The Morningstar ownership table contains a row larger than the entire share count and overlapping manager/subfund hierarchies; no flow or control inference is drawn. FCF widgets are inconsistent and economically weak for a deposit-funded bank, so no industrial FCF/EV-based valuation is used. Provider moat, uncertainty, capital-allocation and ESG labels are opinions, not guarantees of low share-price loss risk.

Next questions: how much wealth growth is net flows; what recurring CNB return follows required remediation; which vintages explain impaired formation; how much HSBC revenue is incremental; and what return hurdle governs repurchases near 3× common book?

The 2.67× P/B discrepancy

At C$96.73 current common book value, P/B is approximately 2.895×. Dividing common market value by total equity of C$145,094m gives about 2.67×, but includes other capital interests. Separately, C$280.01 divided by the public FY2027 forecast BVPS of C$105 also gives 2.67×. Those are different denominators; a matching number does not make the methods equivalent. The forward P/E and common P/B/ROE combination carry the most weight. A 20× trailing P/E can reflect temporarily depressed profits; a low P/E can reflect peak-cycle profits. The denominator must be sustainable.

Why the history does not time the sale

The annual financial results were published after the corresponding fiscal year-end prices. Treating these observations as information available for a contemporaneous trade would introduce look-ahead bias. IFRS changes, insurance accounting, acquisitions and business mix further limit comparability. This is not a daily forward-consensus dataset.

FY2024 ended around 14.97× annual earnings. FY2025’s closing price still rose 22.0% as annual EPS increased approximately 25.1%. Earnings growth can absorb a high starting multiple.

Issuer tables support a 2020 high/low comparison of C$109.68 to C$72.00 (−34.4%) and a 2007-to-Q2-2009 comparison of C$61.08 to C$25.52 (−58.2%). These are ordered intraday period highs/lows, not a reconstructed daily closing-price maximum drawdown. They show that large losses can occur; they do not calibrate a present-day threshold.

The new one-, three- and five-year forward-P/E study adds a limited dividend-reinvestment history and chronological prediction screen. Complete point-in-time estimates, verified publication lags and independent cycle coverage remain unavailable. It does not establish a “very likely” fall threshold or assign fall probabilities.

TEST

Forward P/E and subsequent returns: which horizon matters?

↑

The three-year horizon is the best-supported research choice among one, three and five years in the available data. It has the strongest relationship on identical entry dates and the largest improvement over a historical-mean baseline in a small walk-forward screen. That selects a useful lens; it does not establish a reliable forecast at today’s valuation.

How to read the result

Three years explains 63.9% of return variation in the matched 38-entry comparison. The calculator below uses all 46 mature three-year observations, where R² is 32.9%. The higher comparison figure is not the calculator’s full-sample fit and neither percentage is a probability of being right.

Open the forward-P/E calculator

A fair horizon comparison uses the same entry dates

Five-year outcomes require older starting dates. Comparing only the largest available sample at each horizon would mix a horizon effect with different market periods. The primary comparison uses the same 38 entry dates, November 29, 2010 to July 30, 2021, with fully observed one-, three- and five-year total returns.

Identical entry dates; cumulative CAD total returns with dividends reinvested
HorizonMatched entriesPearson rMatched-entry R²Test error reduction
1 year38-0.51526.6%+16.22%
3 years · selected38-0.79963.9%+54.12%
5 years38-0.34211.7%−7.60%

Test error reduction = 1 − model squared error / historical-mean squared error. Positive is better than the baseline; negative is worse. The 54.1% three-year result means a reduction in squared error, not 54.1% forecast accuracy. All horizons use the same 10 overlapping test entries.

What the walk-forward check actually tests

At each test entry, training uses only observations whose entire holding-period return had already ended on or before that date. Each horizon needs at least 12 training observations. The shared test dates run from April 30, 2019 to July 30, 2021. The baseline is the mean return of that horizon’s available training sample, re-estimated each time.

Inspect the chronological prediction rule
For each test entry t:
Training = entries before t whose exit date is on or before t
Fit: holding-period total return (%) = a + b × entry forward P/E
Model prediction[t] = a + b × forward P/E[t]
Baseline prediction[t] = mean(training holding-period returns)
Test skill = 1 − Σ(actual − model prediction)² / Σ(actual − baseline)²

The test prevents return outcomes from extending beyond their forecast date in the training set. It does not independently verify historical consensus-estimate vintages. Ten overlapping three-year tests contain only one greedily selected disjoint holding window. Disjoint does not guarantee economic independence. The screen also helps choose among three candidates, so it is not an untouched final validation set.

Download every shared test prediction

Three years remains first when minimum training counts change to 10 or 15. The strictest check contains only five test entries; these are sensitivity analyses, not independent validations.

Training-size sensitivity; the 12-observation minimum is the primary screen

Later observations weaken the apparent predictability

Using all 26 available three-year walk-forward test entries reduces squared error by 28.6%. In the eight entries after the shared test period, the improvement falls to 12.3%. The final July 2023 entry returned about 149% over three years, compared with the historical model’s roughly 50% walk-forward estimate. The model can miss a strong outcome by a wide margin.

Source and sampling choices matter

Earlier Yahoo archive52.6% (n=15)56.5% (n=15)68.9% (n=15)

The earlier Yahoo subset favours five years on in-sample fit; the later GuruFocus series favours three years. The pooled choice is not a permanent law for RBC. All matched-cohort slopes stay negative when any one entry year is removed, but omitted variables and changes in the business or market can still alter the relationship.

Data construction, coverage and uncertainty

The public valuation universe contains 58 distinct quarterly entries. It combines 15 eligible archived Yahoo quarters before 2016 with the original GuruFocus series; 54, 46 and 38 entries have matured for one, three and five years respectively. No missing P/E is interpolated, and no later realized EPS is substituted for a historical forecast.

The selected three-year sample has six missing quarters within its entry span: 2011 Q3, 2012 Q4, 2014 Q2, 2015 Q1, 2015 Q3 and 2015 Q4. Earlier archived TSX pages from 2004, 2005, 2007 and 2008 lack a usable forward P/E. A 2015 annual screen was excluded because its stated-date closing price did not reconcile. This is incomplete history, with no 2007–2009 entry observations.

Return construction and date mapping
Daily wealth factor = (close[d] + cash dividend[d]) / close[d −1]
Wealth[d] = cumulative product of daily wealth factors
Holding-period total return (%) = 100 × (Wealth[exit] / Wealth[entry] − 1)
Annualized observed return (%) = 100 × ((1 + total return / 100)^(1 / years) − 1)

Returns are nominal CAD for the Toronto-listed shares. Dividends are fractionally reinvested on ex-dates at the daily close, a research approximation rather than the issuer’s actual DRIP execution price. Taxes, fees and withholding are excluded. GuruFocus month labels are mapped to calendar month-end and the last trading close on or before it. Yahoo archive captures are converted to Toronto time; use the first trading close on or after capture, advancing for captures after 4 p.m. Eastern. Exit uses the trading close on or before the calendar anniversary. Price outcomes end October 16, 2026. Historical forecast vintages and exact observation timestamps remain imperfect.

GuruFocus · TSX RY forward P/E Yahoo Finance · RY.TO historical prices and dividends Original Yahoo RY.TO statistics · archived example

Yahoo labels a fiscal-year forecast endpoint, sometimes more than 12 months ahead. GuruFocus permits next-twelve-month or next-fiscal-year forecasts; its historical vintages are not independently verified. The comparison therefore remains exploratory, despite chronological outcome filtering.

The 38 matched entries contain only 10, 4, 3 greedily selected disjoint holding windows for one, three and five years. For the full three-year fit, residual RMSE is 20.42 percentage points; an approximate calendar-time HAC slope interval is -21.94 to -11.13 percentage points per P/E turn. The Bartlett bandwidth is three calendar years with an n/(n −2) correction. These approximate intervals do not solve source breaks, overlap, missing cycles or forecast selection. No calibrated return interval or crash probability is supplied.

The earlier calculator fitted annualized returns and compounded the fitted annual mean. That is a different model: a nonlinear conversion of a fitted mean does not equal the fitted mean of the transformed outcome. The direct cumulative model is retained here to answer the holding-period return question consistently. Separately fitting annualized outcomes does not change the horizon ranking in the matched sample. R² measures in-sample variation, not accuracy or the probability of a fall.

ROE

What 2.9× book requires

↑

A premium P/B is a claim on the bank’s ability to earn above its required equity return. The stability and duration of that excess profitability matter more than book value alone.

Justified P/B ≈ (sustainable ROE − g) / (required equity return − g)
Stable-growth model sensitivities; all inputs are assumptions
Sustainable ROERequired returnPerpetual growthImplied P/B
18%10%4%2.33×
18%9%4%2.80×
18%10%6%3.00×

At current common P/B of 2.89× and 4% perpetual growth, the model implies sustainable ROE of 21.4% at a 10% required return, or 18.5% at 9%. Latest adjusted quarterly ROE is 18.1%; a single annualized quarter is not a perpetual forecast.

Reverse the P/B equation
ROE = g + (P/B × (kₑ − g))
At kₑ = 10%, g = 4%:
ROE = 4% + (2.894886 × 6%) = 21.3693%
At kₑ = 9%, g = 4%:
ROE = 4% + (2.894886 × 5%) = 18.4744%

This is a steady-state diagnostic, not a point price target. It assumes consistent equity and earnings definitions, clean-surplus accounting, stable distributions/reinvestment, and kₑ > g. A credible multistage path can produce a different value. A higher perpetual growth assumption is not a costless way to justify a higher multiple.

Aswath Damodaran, NYU Stern: financial-service firms RBC Q3 2026 Earnings Release

A one percentage point change in required return changes the valuation materially. Better operating durability or a lower risk premium can support a re-rating; weaker sustainable ROE, a higher required return or fading growth can remove it.

Calculate the return hurdle
Required exit price = entry × (1 + hurdle) − dividends
For a 10% one-year return:
280.01 × 1.10 − 7.04 = C$300.971

Required exit EPS at 15× = 300.971 / 15 = C$20.0647

At a 14× exit multiple, the 10% hurdle requires earnings above the public estimate. At 16×, the estimate can be sufficient, but the valuation premium must persist. These are one-year holding-period returns, not discounted multi-year targets.

FUND

The business is strong; watch the composition

↑
RBC Q3 2026 operating and risk indicators
IndicatorLatest reportedInterpretation
Quarterly net incomeC$6.024bnStrong current earnings
Adjusted diluted EPSC$4.28Up 11% year over year
Reported / adjusted ROE17.9% / 18.1%Supports a quality premium
CET1 capital ratio13.5%Capital strength is distinct from equity valuation
Gross impaired loan ratio0.91% vs 0.85% year earlierDeteriorating, but not proof of an earnings breakdown

Adjusted efficiency ratio52.2%Cost discipline supports profitability
Adjusted operating leverage+2.4%Revenue growth exceeded adjusted expense growth

Wealth Management plus Capital Markets generated C$1,442m + C$1,544m = C$2,986m, or 49.6% of C$6,024m group net income. Both contain recurring businesses, but market appreciation, trading activity and transactions influence results. Personal Banking net income fell 1% year over year. The mix of growth matters.

OSFI’s generic large-bank CET1 expectation is 11.0%, including the 3% Domestic Stability Buffer. RBC’s rounded bank-specific requirement is 11.1% including its countercyclical increment, leaving 240bps to its 13.5% reported ratio. This regulatory comparison is broader than capital available above management’s operating buffers. A planned use of capital for growth or distributions is different from unexpected erosion caused by losses.

Macro factors must translate into bank earnings

The Bank of Canada held its policy rate at 2.25% on September 2. Lower rates do not automatically improve bank margins: asset repricing, deposit costs, hedges and funding mix interact. Monitor unemployment, mortgage renewals, commercial real estate, unsecured credit and City National, alongside segment net interest margins.

Trade disruption, energy-price inflation and geopolitical uncertainty can pressure both credit assumptions and the equity risk premium. These are transmission channels to monitor, not quantified predictions in this note.

What must be true for the premium to hold

  • Earnings estimates remain credible and execution supports the growth path.
  • ROE stays sufficiently strong to justify the common-book premium.
  • Credit losses remain manageable without relying indefinitely on reserve releases.
  • Expense discipline and capital generation support sustainable distributions.

Concentrated owner

A partial sale can reduce risk now. Size it against an intended portfolio weight. Approximate shares to sell = (current RBC value − target weight × portfolio value) / price, before tax and costs, assuming proceeds remain in the portfolio.

Long-term, appropriately sized owner

A high multiple alone does not establish the right position size. Retain exposure only if the required growth, likely volatility and downside fit the mandate. Redirecting new purchases limits further concentration but does not reduce shares already held.

Thesis deterioration

Reassess even after the price falls. A stock can become more expensive on P/E if earnings estimates fall faster than the quotation. Waiting to recover a former peak can prolong a broken investment thesis.

Timing, dividends and execution

The next scheduled RBC results call is December 3, 2026, 8:30 a.m. ET. It is an evidence checkpoint; the research establishes no advantage to selling immediately before or after the release. The declared dividend has an October 26 record date and November 24 payment date. Waiting for a dividend creates no free return: value leaves the company, while other information also moves the price.

A 10–15% trailing stop is a trading choice. Normal volatility can trigger it; a gap can execute below the stop, and a stop-limit may not fill. Portfolio-weight rebalancing may provide more predictable concentration control. Cash needed soon is a separate reason to reduce market exposure.

For a non-registered account, selling can realize a gain or loss. Under the general current rule, a 50% capital-gains inclusion rate means half the gain enters taxable income, not that the tax rate is 50%. Registered-account trading differs from withdrawals. Employee holdings may have plan, vesting or trading-window restrictions; those require an individual review.

Scope, evidence and analytical limits

↑

This is independent, public-source equity research. It is not issued by RBC, Bloomberg or an investment bank and does not imply affiliation, licensed market-data access or a broker recommendation. It supplies a dated valuation framework rather than a formally underwritten price target or a personalized instruction.

Issuer filings control reported facts. Issuer-based original forecasts are presented separately from public market-data and estimate displays. Source and assumption dates remain distinct. Important inputs are labelled reported, provider estimate, derived calculation or analytical assumption. The estimate providers’ adjustment bases and forecast horizons are not fully exposed; this caps confidence in comparisons.

The senior cases explicitly use 30/50/20 judgment weights, not measured or statistically calibrated probabilities. Their weighted value is an illustration of assumed asymmetry. The original supplemental provider cases remain unweighted; the return-study regression is a separate historical association. These methods are not combined into a single forecast. The added dividend-reinvestment study is an exploratory association and chronology-controlled screen, not a validated point-in-time threshold backtest. A normalized six-bank forecast model and current individual portfolio/tax information are unavailable. These gaps prevent a precise “best day,” guaranteed sale price or claim that a fall is very likely above one multiple.

For banks, sustainable common earnings, ROE, common book, asset quality and regulatory capital take priority. Conventional industrial-company P/OCF, EV/EBITDA and net-debt rules are weak fits because funding is part of operations. PEG adds an uncertain growth denominator and ignores credit-cycle risk.

What would change the conclusion?

Higher sustainable earnings and book growth, stronger operating durability or a lower justified required return can support today’s premium. Persistent downgrades, weaker ROE and unexpected credit/capital stress strengthen the sale case. Update the denominators before moving any review band.
